analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts and the bounded addition patch for provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. The added test at HEAD 3140 onward checks that maintenance revalidates ownership after header corruption despite restored mtime, preserves the now-unowned file, and does not count it toward TTL/budget deletion. The partial following test covers replacement of a malformed lookalike with an owned block. These are defensive assertions, not evidence of a new runtime vulnerability.
BASE 3039–3290 covers successor-epoch preservation, temp-byte accounting, malformed-file preservation, symlink rejection, exact temp ownership and periodic cleanup. BASE 3293–3728 covers donation benefit/staging/rate/queue bounds and outcome accounting. BASE 3731–4237 covers sliding-window geometry, HMAC domain/scope separation, metadata commitments and AAD compatibility, restart recovery, incomplete/corrupt-window fallback and default-off sidecars. These relate chiefly to T-041, TB-007, TB-003, A-001 and availability; the supplied changes do not alter authorization, attestation, transport encryption or billing.
No concrete regression is supported in this test-only scope. Integration should verify any associated SSDWholeRootMaintainer ownership-verdict caching implementation: cached verdicts must invalidate on file replacement or content/status changes and remain compatible with no-follow traversal, TTL and disk-budget accounting. That implementation and the remainder of the addition patch are not supplied here; tests alone cannot establish those properties. Existing sidecar behavior and nil-scope fixtures are BASE behavior, not newly introduced exposure.
